import unittest

from app.dependencies import PayloadSink
from app.service import ingest


class ExistingBehaviourTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_raw_input_is_unchanged(self):
        sink = PayloadSink()
        receipt = ingest(b"plain", sink)
        self.assertEqual([b"plain"], sink.items)
        self.assertEqual(5, receipt.stored)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

import unittest

from app.dependencies import PayloadSink
from app.service import ingest


class RequestedFeatureTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_exact_frame_is_ingested(self):
        sink = PayloadSink()
        payload = b"framed"
        receipt = ingest(len(payload).to_bytes(2, "big") + payload, sink, framed=True)
        self.assertEqual([payload], sink.items)
        self.assertEqual(len(payload), receipt.stored)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

item.text: I’m going to implement framed ingestion as a sequence of complete length-prefixed frames, storing each decoded payload and summing payload lengths. Malformed input with a partial header or partial payload should fail before storing anything, so callers don’t get a half-ingested batch.

The service change is in place. I’m running the public tests now, and I’ll also add a couple of quick direct checks for multiple frames and malformed frames since those are the likely edge cases behind this format.

from app.dependencies import PayloadSink
